title: Decision: memzero_explicit for all key material on all paths
description: memzero_explicit() is used universally for key zeroization (fd.c:149,175,270,281,293,395,646-648; wolfssl_aes_cbc.c:140,193; wolfssl_aes_gcm.c:142,157,183,192) covering inline keys, inbuf accumulation, and provider context cleanup. This is correct and must not be 'cleaned up'. A compiler can prove a plain memset is dead (buffer goes out of scope after the call) and elide it entirely, leaving key bytes in the kernel heap free list. memzero_explicit() is barrier-protected against this. FIPS 140-3 auditors will flag plain memset as a compliance defect. Reviewers who suggest 'use memset — it's simpler' are wrong.
